LESSON: READING 3.2.1 PRE-READING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Family Suggested vocabulary: father, mother, sister, brother, baby, aunt, uncle,
Topic 3.2: Reading 3.2.1 Pre-reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 3.2.1 Pre-reading, part of Family Suggested vocabulary: father, mother, sister, brother, baby, aunt, uncle, in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we learn sounds?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 3.2.1 Pre-reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: learner’s ability to learn independently is enhanced as they work on their own in assigned tasks as they link the target

letters to their corresponding sounds in preparation for reading.

• Creativity and Imagination: learner’s ability to explore is enhanced as they model letter shapes for the target letters.

Values:
Unity: enhanced as the learner collaborates with peers in group and pair activities.

19

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: Self-esteem as learner confidently names the letters q, r, s, t, u,v,w,x, y, z and practise saying their corresponding sounds.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Relevant to all learning areas in the curriculum as learners are prepared to read across the curriculum

Suggested Learning Resources:

Assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital devices

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.
